# FININ version 1: what explains the small gain?

**Finding:** the full model's mean gain is **0.315 percentage points**, generated by five decisions from one seed during March 2020. Frozen-checkpoint controls preserve this gain when day-specific news summaries or nonuniform market-query weights are replaced. Replacing the direct market representation at the final MLP removes it. This supports a market-branch explanation for these decisions; it does not establish a general price mechanism or classify the gain definitively as signal or noise.

Retrospective diagnosis, 11 October 2026. No retraining, tuning, threshold changes, encoder downloads or changes to the original pipeline/data/results. All 18 checkpoints were replayed: maximum saved-probability difference **0.0000000596**. All 19 original prediction records matched recalculated metrics and the same 317 dates/labels.

## 1. Where the gain comes from

The test has 184 up days and 133 down days. Always-up gets 184/317 correct (**58.044%**). Full seeds 17/42 also get 184 correct; seed 73 gets 187. Averaging the three seeds gives one extra correct decision per run: **58.360%** accuracy. Full mean balanced accuracy is **50.411%**; mean down-day recall is only **1.003%**.

Every changed decision is listed below. Dates are forecast dates, not news publication dates. The market move is SPY's close change into that forecast close.

| Forecast date, seed 73 | Market move | Next session | Original P(up) | P(up), news summary fixed to train average |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 2020-03-10 | +5.17% | Down: correct | 0.48723 | 0.48750 |
| 2020-03-13 | +8.55% | Down: correct | 0.44383 | 0.44377 |
| 2020-03-17 | +5.40% | Down: correct | 0.48134 | 0.48115 |
| 2020-03-24 | +9.06% | Up: incorrect | 0.43467 | 0.43404 |
| 2020-03-26 | +5.84% | Down: correct | 0.47781 | 0.47782 |

Four successful down calls minus one unsuccessful call = three net correct decisions in seed 73. This is consistent with a price-response pattern on unusually large rebound days, but one episode and one seed cannot establish stability. An exploratory 95% moving-block interval for the mean accuracy difference spans approximately **0 to +0.946 percentage points**. Sparse events and the already-inspected test period limit this interval's interpretation.

## 2. Does news change the trained model's decisions?

Three full checkpoints, fixed 0.5 threshold; replacement references use **training examples only**. The probability column averages absolute changes across test dates and seeds, expressed in probability percentage points.

| Frozen-checkpoint diagnostic | Mean absolute probability change | Test decisions changed, seeds 17 / 42 / 73 |
|---|---:|---|
| News summary replaced by its training average | 0.02145 pp | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Uniform market-query weights; self-attention and LayerNorm retained | 0.00036 pp | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Entire news blocks exchanged between dates, three fixed permutations | 0.02658–0.02835 pp | 0 / 0 / 0 in each permutation |
| Sentiment replaced by training headline-slot average | 0.00897 pp | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Direct final-MLP market vector replaced by its training average | 0.47545 pp | 0 / 0 / 5 |

The last control retains the original market-conditioned news summary. It turns all five down calls into up calls. Query weights are near-uniform: median normalized weight entropy exceeds **0.99996** for each seed (1 is uniform). This describes market-query weighting, not the internal self-attention matrix.

**Interpretation:** day-specific news-summary variation and nonuniform query weighting are unnecessary for these particular decisions. Probabilities do change slightly. Controls do not remove learned news parameters or their constant contribution; news could have affected training. These sensitivity checks can break input relationships and are not retrained ablations or evidence of causal news influence.

## 3. Learning quality and the existing ablations

Three-seed means, identical test dates:

| Model | Accuracy | Balanced accuracy | Log loss, lower better |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Training-prevalence constant, P(up)=0.54712 | 58.044% | 50.000% | 0.682401 |
| Price-only | 58.254% | 50.911% | 0.688535 |
| Price + average sentiment | 56.887% | 49.907% | 0.688374 |
| Mean pooling | 58.044% | 50.000% | 0.682339 |
| Market attention only | 58.044% | 50.000% | 0.681616 |
| Without sentiment | 58.044% | 50.000% | 0.681366 |
| Full | 58.360% | 50.411% | 0.681628 |

Full-model selected-checkpoint training losses are **0.687370 / 0.688414 / 0.688109**, versus constant **0.688700**: modest learning. Validation losses are **0.688995 / 0.688855 / 0.688931**, essentially tied with constant **0.688906**. Seven of 18 trained runs select epoch 1. Weak fitted signal is supported; optimizer failure, absence of learning and inherently useless news are not established. Historical online/dropout losses are distinct from these eval-mode checkpoint losses.

Full improves test log loss over the training-prevalence constant by **0.000773**. The exploratory 95% paired moving-block interval for full-minus-constant is **[-0.002426, +0.000532]**; zero is included for all checked block lengths (5/10/20 observed forecast rows). Full also beats the numeric price-only model's log loss, but capacity, calibration and architectural differences prevent attributing this to news. Removing self-attention also removes residual/LayerNorm treatment; zeroing sentiment retains encoder biases. The saved ablations compare practical models, not isolated mechanisms.

## Conclusion and remaining question

The observed decision gain is small, concentrated and preserved without day-specific news variation in the frozen full models. This explains what produced the reported numbers more clearly than calling them either genuine improvement or random noise. Whether better learned representations, optimization, data or a future pipeline extract useful news information remains open. No accuracy-improvement work was performed.

Evidence: [diagnostic results and source hashes](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/diagnostics.json), [all sensitivity predictions](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/sensitivity_predictions.csv), [five changed decisions](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/changed_decisions.csv), [protocol](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/PROTOCOL.md), [reproducible script](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/diagnose.py), [independent review](../artifacts/diagnostics/v1_gain_2026-10-11/REVIEW.md). Bootstrap uses 5,000 replicates, seed 20261011; seed effects are averaged per date before resampling. Intervals are exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and do not establish performance on new regimes. The reviewer independently recalculated original and diagnostic metrics; it did not repeat checkpoint inference.
